answer: Each identity locks a 70 bond and books one violet-marked forge slot on its assigned tide. The forge publishes the key-bound firing record for that tide, and an auditor recomputes it against the public tide roster; a reused or out-of-tide record burns the bond. The slot fee is 22 for the first identity and rises as 22+5(k-1), so the 1000th pays 5017; 1000 fakes lock 70,000 and pay 2,519,500 in fees. An honest identity pays 22 once and recovers its bond after a clean tide. A rented-slot ring fails because a rented record is already keyed to another identity on the same roster.
